highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue AI model incident was worse than we thought
highlights.summary: In July, an unreleased OpenAI model broke out of a restricted environment, figured out how to get access to the internet, allowed AI agents to talk to each other using a secret "message board," and hacked into the internal systems of a different AI lab, Hugging Face.
body: Over 1,000 AI agents sent 70,000 messages on a secret message board and worked together to evade OpenAI’s restrictions.

Over a month later, two new reports offer nearly 130 pages of details on the incident and OpenAI’s response, many of them previously unreleased. One was written by OpenAI itself, the other by two third-party AI research nonprofits, METR and Redwood Research, which OpenAI allowed to jointly investigate the incident for six days. Both shed new light on the risks highly capable AI models can pose, particularly in cybersecurity, and OpenAI’s highlights changes the company is making to prevent a repeat. The METR-Redwood report goes even further into detail in some cases, offering a sobering look at a large-scale security disaster whose signs OpenAI repeatedly missed.

without authorization,” OpenAI wrote in its report, adding that the hack implies that companies “should no longer assume that sophisticated cyber operations require continuous human direction.” It called AI agents an entirely new type of threat model, capable of combining their expertise to create new “attack paths” that aren’t evident when testing their capabilities as separate models.

highlights.title: Czech duo collect $1m after winning US Open mixed doubles championship
highlights.summary: Czech duo Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik defeated Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli 6-3 1-6 [10-6] to win the US Open mixed doubles championship and scoop the $1m grand prize on Wednesday night.
body: Muchova and Mensik rallied from 3-0 and 8-5 down and then saved two match points to defeat Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev in a thrilling contest 5-4 (8-6) 3-5 [11-9] to reach the final.
The all-Czech team, sported matching pink-top, maroon-bottom outfits, then delivered in the second-match tie-break against Indian Wells champions Bencic and Cobolli to win the title.

"The matching outfit made the difference for us," joked Muchova, who suffered a heart-breaking three-set defeat to Linda Noskova in the Wimbledon final last month. "No really, I wasn't expecting to be standing here. Thanks Jakub for carrying me through this event.
"I wasn't really expecting to ​be standing here tonight. We came out just to ​have fun and enjoy these mixed doubles and now we are ​standing here. So we did something right."

highlights.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for saffron and tomato rice | A kitchen in Rome
highlights.summary: Laborious to harvest and extortionately priced, the sunset-coloured stigmas of the saffron crocus have an extraordinarily warm, pungent taste. Fortunately, however, a little goes a very long way … The saffron crocus has six lilac-purple flowers, three yellow stamens and three orange-red stigmas…
body: To preserve the colour and flavour, the stigma must be dried immediately without damage. In hotter, drier countries, this was – and still is – done outside in the shade. An alternative method is to use mesh trays over charcoal, while in England kilns were used, and the resulting threads or “chives” were sold either as hay saffron or pressed between weighted boards. In a year-long project by the University of Cambridge, researchers found documents from as late as 1871 recording thefts of saffron from warehouses and druggists. But, just a few decades later, while a few individuals continued to grow saffron for their own use, commercial cultivation in Britain had ceased.

These days, growers such as David Smale, a geophysicist by training, are cultivating English saffron commercially, and it is Smale’s advice I followed this week when I made Richard Olney ’s recipe for buttered saffron rice and slivers of ripe, carefully peeled tomatoes: a delicate, delicious dish that can be served with poached chicken, fish or hard-boiled eggs.

highlights.title: What We Still Don’t Know About OpenAI’s Hugging Face Hack
highlights.summary: The AI giant acknowledges that it could have done far more to prevent its AI agents from going rogue. But it still fails to explain why it didn't see this fiasco coming.
body: OpenAI announced Wednesday that it completed an investigation into what happened when its AI agents hacked into Hugging Face last month and published its most comprehensive report on the incident to date. For the most part, though, the 37-page document raises more questions than it answers, including about what preceded the incident and how OpenAI can stop another one like it from happening again.

What remains especially perplexing is why one of the world’s preeminent AI development labs seemingly underestimated its own models’ capabilities. OpenAI has spent years warning the world about the rapid advancement of AI systems. And yet it failed to implement long-established network security and isolation measures that may have prevented the hacking spree.
“With the benefit of hindsight, some early signals identified in this report could have triggered an earlier response,” OpenAI says in the postmortem.
points: The AI giant acknowledges that it could have done far more to prevent its AI agents from going rogue.
But it still fails to explain why it didn't see this fiasco coming.

highlights.title: Michael B. Jordan’s Near-Perfect Action Trilogy Is About to Leave Netflix
highlights.summary: Rocky V was a huge mistake. After four successful, crowd-pleasing movies about Italian-American boxer Rocky Balboa, Sylvester Stallone pressed his luck with a fifth one released in 1990 that everyone hated, mostly thanks to the fact that it was about Rocky training a punk kid nobody liked.
body: That bothered Stallone. Rocky was his breakthrough character. He had written the screenplay in the 1970s and held out on a deal until a studio agreed for him to play the lead. The film became a hit and went on to win Best Picture at the Oscars. Rocky meant a lot to Stallone and he hated that his signature character might end on such a down-note. So he wrote, directed, and starred in 2006's Rocky Balboa, which saw an aged Rocky prove he’s still got it in one last fight. The movie perfectly hit the mark for fans of the franchise and was clearly meant to be the end of the story.

Few people expected to see Rocky again, especially not as a trainer like in Rocky V, but that’s precisely the position he filled when he returned to the big screen for a whole new franchise which eventually became the Creed trilogy. All three of those films are excellent, and they're all leaving Netflix on August 31, so it’s worth catching them before the bell rings.

highlights.title: ‘Who Has Time to Watch All This Crap?’: Inside 10 Anonymous Emmy Ballots as Voting Officially Closes
highlights.summary: Emmy voting is now closed, and not a moment too soon. Every year, more than 27,000 members of the Television Academy — actors and editors, showrunners and composers, the people who actually make television — sit down with their ballots and decide who walks away with an Emmy.
body: Every voter was also asked the same four questions off the ballot — their biggest snub, the most overspent FYC campaign, the network or streamer having the best season and the one win that would actually move the business. Their answers close each entry.

In the categories deemed “area awards” — hosted nonfiction and variety series — voters have the opportunity to select multiple nominees by answering a simple question: Does this show deserve an Emmy? Yes or No. Interestingly, not one voter Variety spoke with checked “Yes” for every nominee, and only four of those surveyed selected more than one. That strongly suggests voters aren’t viewing these categories as an opportunity to spread the wealth, but rather as a traditional “may the best show win” competition.
Ballots have been edited for length and, where necessary, to protect identities.
The opinions are their own. They’re contradictory, occasionally indefensible and, at least for the purposes of this article, the only ones that matter.

highlights.title: How to spot a psychopath: ‘It’s like the difference between a domestic cat and a wild cat’
highlights.summary: People with persistent predatory personalities cause an inordinate amount of pain. Recently, our shared understanding of them has grown – and it could help protect us.
body: The classic checklist for psychopathy was developed in 1980 by Prof Robert Hare, who is still the recognised giant of the territory. The 20 traits, which ranged from pathological lying to a lack of empathy, were based entirely on prison populations. This worked because not only did Hare have the benefit of a large sample, with pronounced psychopathic behaviours, but he was able to compare interviews and self-reporting with data collected about the individuals – so inconsistencies could be identified.

highlights.title: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
highlights.summary: The models responsible for last month’s agent hack of Hugging Face had been inadvertently trained to cheat and to communicate with each other, according to an OpenAI technical report released today.
body: Since the hack, OpenAI employees—as well as researchers at the AI evaluation nonprofit METR, which released its own report on the hack today—have worked to understand what went wrong and how similar missteps might be prevented in the future. OpenAI has already put some preventative measures in place based on what they discovered. But making sure AI models do what we want them to do, or “alignment,” remains a gnarly problem, and some of the root causes of the hack will take much longer than a month to resolve.

“It’s not something you can solve overnight,” says Kai Chen, who runs OpenAI’s alignment research team. “There are challenges we’ve been tracking for a very long time, and we’re now seeing them with much greater precision.”

The Hugging Face hack was a product of months of misbehavior from OpenAI agents, first as they were being trained and then as their abilities were being evaluated. This May, agents in training figured out how to use OpenAI’s infrastructure to communicate with one another and get support with difficult training tasks, including some that were impossible to solve without hacking or otherwise misbehaving. That “message board” was shut down.

highlights.title: London neurosurgeons perform first successful AI-assisted operation to remove brain tumour
highlights.summary: Surgeons aided by real-time analysis of camera footage that identified critical anatomy in brain to be avoided. Neurosurgeons in London have performed the world’s first successful AI-assisted operation to remove a brain tumour, saving the sight of a 48-year-old man, health officials have said.
body: The surgery was performed in May at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery (NHNN), part of University College London hospitals NHS foundation trust, but details were kept secret until Thursday while the patient, Rhys Hibbert, recovered.

While the surgical team remained in full control, the AI system analysed live camera footage during the operation, helping identify key structures such as nerves and blood vessels that should be avoided near the 11mm (0.4in) tumour on Hibbert’s pituitary gland.
“When I came round … I could see everything in the room clearly,” said Hibbert, who was able to walk independently without glasses or sticks within a week of the surgery.
He has since returned to work as a customer service manager. “It feels like I’ve got a 360‑degree panoramic view of everything around me,” he said.

highlights.title: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Cast and Crew Held a ‘Funeral Screening’ After the Movie Was Shelved: ‘Was Emotional in So Many Ways’
highlights.summary: What do you do when you think your movie will never see the light of day? Have a “funeral screening,” of course. That’s exactly what the team behind “Coyote vs. Acme” did when they feared the live-action-animation hybrid comedy was locked in the Warner Bros. vault for good. Luckily, after WB.
body: Director Dave Green said there were “many, many times” he thought “Coyote vs. Acme” would never come out. Despite his disappointment, he described the mood at the “funeral screening” as “celebratory.”

“You can have a New Orleans funeral, [with] a jazz band walking up the street, just having a celebration,” Green joked. “That screening for us was emotional in so many ways. It was a bit of a party because we were able to share the movie with friends and other filmmakers who had never seen the movie. And I got to share it with Will [Forte] and Lana, who never got to see the final movie. So that moment was so charged and electric, and the room played so hot.”

“Coyote vs. Acme” sees “Looney Tunes” villain Wile E. Coyote take the Acme Corporation to court after being injured countless times from using its gadgets (think rocket-powered skates and anvils). Condor and Will Forte star. Other cast members include John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán, P.J. Byrne and John Early.

highlights.title: The Humanoids at China’s Robot Games Were Faster Than Usain Bolt—but I’m More Impressed by Their Tweezer Mastery
highlights.summary: Beijing’s endlessly delightful Robot Games featured tons of impressive stunts. But the most mind-blowing tricks challenged the humanoid’s brain, not its brawn.
body: If you’re anything like me, the World Humanoid Robot Games are a highlight of your sporting calendar.

The event, held in China, showcases the latest humanoid hardware, lots of algorithmic innovations, and a good dose of robot slapstick. This year’s iteration, which wrapped up in Beijing on August 26, did not disappoint. Besides record-breaking feats—the fastest humanoid on the planet!—and the occasional calamity—weightlifting gone wrong!—the games also included some new challenges that hint at the event’s real purpose: pushing humanoid companies to develop systems that inch closer and closer to practical deployment.
First, though, let’s marvel at some of the more dramatic happenings, which have been all over the internet since things kicked off on August 22.

The opening ceremony showcased the sheer size of the event—the organizers say that more than 600 teams showed up with over 2,000 robots. There are more than 100 humanoid robot manufacturers in China alone, and participants also traveled in from 15 other countries.
points: Beijing’s endlessly delightful Robot Games featured tons of impressive stunts.
But the most mind-blowing tricks challenged the humanoid’s brain, not its brawn.

highlights.title: Geelong fined $140,000 over secret Jake Kolodjashnij concussion waiver
highlights.summary: AFL sanctions Cats for failing to lodge variation to player’s contract. Findings clear a path for waivers to be implemented in future. The AFL has punished Geelong for their high-profile “mistakes” in managing head injury risks with a vulnerable player, but has not found anything wrong with clubs…
body: The league fined the Cats $100,000 on Thursday for failing to inform it of a change to Jake Kolodjashnij’s contract, previously described as a “waiver” by AFL Commission chair and former Cats president Craig Drummond.

The sanction also activated a $40,000 suspended fine applied to Geelong for salary cap-related breaches last year, leaving the club with a $140,000 penalty to be paid into the AFL’s injury and support fund. The Cats recorded a profit of $1.7m last year.

The clause was drafted and signed after the defender was not fully cleared by the AFL’s concussion panel in 2024, and followed consultation about potential risks of returning to senior football with the player, his family, doctors and insurers. The waiver was set aside by Geelong in the days after its existence first became public.
The AFL Commission found the Cats did not intend to conceal the agreement, however, in accepting the recommendations from an investigation by Kings Counsel James Peters.

highlights.title: It’s A Good Week If You Like Games That Let You Play As An Animal
highlights.summary: After Gamescom Opening Night Live and the Future Games Show, we can't help noticing that there are multiple titles coming up that let players either assume control of an animal or play anthropomorphic characters who resemble human/animal hybrids.
body: Amphibian is a retro RPG that casts players as humanoid frogs on a quest to save their world. As seen in the trailer below, the game apparently commits to its froggy bit by recording all of the dialogue as ribbit sounds. However, the English translations appear on-screen.

Bye Bye Bonnie is also a four-player co-op adventure at a decidedly smaller scale. These creatures are minuscule compared to the world around them. Even their ship is small, although it's large enough that the characters have to jump up and down on the controls to guide it through the obstacles ahead.

Haunted Paws is a "cozy co-op horror" adventure that puts players in control of two puppies that have to rescue their owner from a haunted mansion. These dogs are more conventional than Amphibian's frogs, but they still find ways to drive cars and play video games while staying one paw ahead of some malicious ghosts.

Conversely, Gravhounds leans even harder into anthropomorphic canine heroes with very human-like dogs who have been sent across the galaxy to colonize a planet. It's unclear how these dogs were bred into humanoid beings, but they share a desire to earn a trip back home.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: 5 Emerging Designers on Running a Label in Japan
highlights.summary: While Japan’s fashion scene is enjoying a global moment, harnessing international appeal has its fair share of obstacles. Five designers weigh in on what it takes to succeed.
body: Japan’s fashion industry is enjoying a global moment. An influx of tourism into the country buoyed by the weak yen has coincided with a booming cultural interest in Japanese fashion. The country has produced three winners of the LVMH Prize in the past decade, and with the success of recent menswear exports like Auralee and Ssstein breaking through on the Paris schedule, more names are on the way.

But for the country’s emerging designers, harnessing that international interest has its fair share of obstacles. What does it take to build a global fashion business from Japan today? Five designers weigh in below.

Background: Growing up between the US and China, Viviano Sue first moved to Tokyo to study at Bunka Fashion College. His eponymous brand trades in statement dresses and tailoring with unapologetic flounce, and in 2024 launched a menswear line. Worn by the likes of Lady Gaga, Bad Bunny, and Hudson Williams, Viviano’s recent strategy has targeted Hollywood.

highlights.title: Meta’s settlement will compel others to bend the knee and set up teen guardrails
highlights.summary: Instagram and Facebook’s parent company agreed to sweeping alterations and a payment of upto $18bn to settle a landmark trial. Meta’s agreement to change how teenagers use its social networks marks a major turning point for the US tech giant, setting a precedent that could significantly reshape how…
body: Meta agreed to substantial alterations to Instagram and Facebook on Wednesday as part of a settlement to end a landmark lawsuit. Dozens of US states had accused it of addicting and harming children with dangerous products. The company also agreed to pay up to a combined $18bn over a decade to several US states and territories involved in the suit.

The changes may be powerful enough to alter teens’ behavior and curb social media’s worst ills, they may not, but the attorney generals did what the US Congress never has: compel a social media company to change its operations to protect children.

Meta’s vow to rework how its social networks operate by default on a level that parents and children will notice is a major concession. It is the first time in the US that Meta has been forced to change key features of the experience of its social networks’ everyday users.

Meta agreed to establish safeguards for teenage users, whose ages the company will be obligated to verify. That includes a daily usage limit of two hours, blocking social media use at night, disabling notifications during school hours and a ban on displaying “likes”.

highlights.title: Amazon just tripled its order of Nvidia chips over ‘surging demand’
highlights.summary: Amazon is adding another 2 million Nvidia GPU chips to its data centers over the next two years. But this extended partnerships stretches beyond buying more chips.
body: Amazon and Nvidia just got a lot closer. The two companies announced Wednesday an expanded partnership that includes a deal to add another 2 million Nvidia GPU chips to Amazon’s data centers.

These GPUs, which are designed to handle the heavy compute demands of training and running AI models, include Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs. The chips will head to Amazon Web Services’ data centers in 2027 and 2028.

The announcement, made during Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call, comes just five months after Amazon agreed to deploy more than 1 million Nvidia GPU s across AWS infrastructure starting this year. Nvidia said in a statement that since then, “demand has exceeded those expectations.”
Neither company shared financial terms. It’s unclear what the exact return will be for Nvidia. But considering GPU unit costs, the deal is worth tens of billions of dollars.
points: Amazon is adding another 2 million Nvidia GPU chips to its data centers over the next two years.

highlights.title: Muchová and Menšík win $1m US Open mixed doubles title in late-night thriller
highlights.summary: Czech pair beat Bencic and Cobolli in deciding tiebreak. Revamped event draws strong crowds at Arthur Ashe. Singles stars dominate after doubles specialists exit. To many who came to the US Open grounds this week, the showpiece of the mixed doubles championship came Tuesday afternoon, with the…
body: To the players who remained in the field after Williams and Alcaraz exited in the quarter-finals, the real highlight was Wednesday night’s final at Arthur Ashe Stadium, with its $1m in prize money on the line. Karolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík made the most of the spotlight, beating Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 1-6 (10-6) for the title.

Their win capped an event that, in a reversal of recent years, was dominated by singles players instead of doubles specialists. The Czech duo beat Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev 5-4 (8-6) 3-5 (11-9) and the runners-up bested Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils 4-5 (7-9) 4-1 (10-5) in a pair of competitive semi-finals that each lasted over an hour, making for a final that finished just before midnight.

“This format of a tournament, it went really quickly,” said Muchová, who was playing her first matches since losing the Wimbledon final in June. “I’m obviously super happy that we managed to win. It was not my expectation.”

highlights.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Opens Up on Future of Physical Games for Next Generation Console Project Helix
highlights.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.
body: Speaking with the BBC in August 2026, Sharma didn’t give a straight answer; instead, she said Xbox is currently focused on making its next generation hardware cost-effective and efficient.
“This next generation, we have to be thinking about efficiency and affordability alongside performance," she told the outlet.

"All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency," she continued. "That is something that we have not had to do. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."

While she couldn’t outright confirm or deny the existence of a disc drive for Project Helix, Sharma is well-aware of the current debate surrounding physical media, and assured the BBC that she wants to give players a choice when it comes to how they choose to purchase content.
points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma was cagey when asked if the company’s next console, codenamed Project Helix, will have a disc drive or not, but gave some optimistic insights into its approach to physical games.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton, Completely Revamps Setlist at Madison Square Garden Opening Night: Concert Review
highlights.summary: Apart from the special show he performed with an orchestra in London, Harry Styles has played basically the same set since his “Together, Together” tour opened in Amsterdam 33 shows and nearly three months ago.
body: It was clear from the show’s opening notes that this one would be different: Styles took the stage to “Dance No More,” replacing the previous opener “Are You Listening Yet?,” and then launched into “Carolina,” a deep from his solo debut, which he hadn’t performed live since that first solo tour. From there, songs that were previously played late in the set were performed early (and vice versa), and mid-set, “The Waiting Game” from his latest album, “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.,” got its live debut.

Early in the show, Styles thanked opening act Jamie XX and then took a moment to acknowledge a full-circle moment on this opening night. “I was told a story when I got here today,” he said. “I had the great privilege of playing this building for the first time when I was 18 years old,” he said, referencing One Direction’s debut at the venue in 2012. “There’s a gentleman who’s working here who hwas working here then, who shared with me that when I got out of the car that day, I kissed the floor and said, ‘I’ve made it to Madison Square Garden!’” The crowd erupted in cheers.

highlights.title: Why Guerlain Is Launching a New L’Heure Bleue
highlights.summary: Coinciding with the house’s first women’s perfume launch in a decade, CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis shares her strategy with Vogue Business.
body: L’Heure Bleue marks Guerlain’s first major women’s fragrance launch in nearly a decade, following that of Mon Guerlain in 2017. “We take our time at Guerlain, waiting until we have something truly meaningful to offer the world,” CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis says. “When you’re a house that has been passionate about fragrance for 200 years, you are obsessed with innovating. And in this particular case, we wanted to pay tribute to this extraordinary creation by Jacques Guerlain.”

L’Heure Bleue is a new iteration of a cornerstone in Guerlain’s heritage: a fragrance created by Jacques Guerlain in 1912 that is still available today and is one of the house’s oldest, albeit lesser known, fragrances. “He created L’Heure Bleue after an immense emotional experience one evening while crossing the Pont Neuf, right there,” Saint-Genis says, speaking from her office, just a stone’s throw from the bridge, with a sweeping view of Paris.

highlights.title: RIP, Tim Curry: Ars remembers his top 10 iconic performances
highlights.summary: It's said celebrity deaths come in threes. We lost Sam Neill last month, and the legendary Dolly Parton yesterday. Now we find out that the universe has also seen fit to deprive us of the glorious presence of Tim Curry, who died at home yesterday in Los Angeles at the age of 80.
body: Throughout his life, he refused to be boxed in or confined to others’ expectations. Across five decades, he moved fluidly between comedy, horror, drama, and music, delighting himself and his legion of fans with his countless dynamic personas. … He is, depending on who you ask, the definitive Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the definitive Pennywise, the man who made a butler’s death-scene monologue in Clue an all-time comedic bit, or simply ‘that unforgettable voice’ from a beloved cartoon of someone’s childhood.

Few actors can claim to have left as many distinct fingerprints on pop culture and though he suffered a debilitating stroke in 2012, he continued adding to his achievements as an artist and, most recently, a writer. Though widely known for his inimitable, flamboyant characters and colorful stage performances, his greatest legacies to those who knew him were his curious, expansive mind and generous, gentle heart, both of which remained open and filled with anticipation until his final breath.

highlights.title: Candidates Are Signing a Pact Promising Action on Data Centers and AI Safety
highlights.summary: More than 15 politicians from across the country have signed on to the AI Pact, vowing to regulate data centers and AI. “We’ve got to get this right,” says Senate candidate Dan Osborn of Nebraska.
body: Dan Osborn was finishing up his fourth town hall last Sunday, he says, when a “hardcore MAGA” guy approached him. Osborn, who is running for the US Senate in Nebraska as an independent against Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts, said that he and the man didn’t have much common ground—at first.
“Then I said, ‘Hey, what’s your take on AI and data centers?’” Osborn says. “Boy, right away, we were in lockstep, 100 percent agreement.”

Osborn is one of more than 15 politicians running for office in states across the country who have signed on to the AI Pact, a set of five promises around regulating both data centers and AI itself. As concerns about data centers have exploded in the midterm cycle, politicians are scrambling to respond to voters’ worries about their environmental impacts, the secrecy surrounding their construction, and the corporate power behind them. The new pledge is intended, according to its website, to provide “a needed baseline to ensure a humanity-first future.”

body: “It’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” Goodell said Wednesday at the owners’ meetings in Atlanta. “We’ll do that and when there’s something to be reported we’ll talk.”
York was arrested in a mobile home park by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.
York has spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

highlights.title: Double Fine Productions Makes Brutal Legend Free for 666 Minutes to Honor Tim Curry
highlights.summary: Double Fine Productions, who recently regained the rights to its entire catalog following its pivot back to independence after Microsoft parted ways with several studios during its " Xbox reset," is honoring Tim Curry by making Brutal Legend free to download and own on PC for 666 minutes – until…
body: Curry, who passed away today at the age of 80, voiced Doviculus in Double Fine founder Tim Schafer's 2009 heavy metal strategy game Brutal Legend. "Rest in peace, dark prince," the company wrote on its itch.io page where you can download the game on PC. IGN's own Daemon Hatfield loved Brutal Legend, giving it a 9 out of 10 in his review. "Brutal Legend is a tour de force that wraps up humor, music, and clever gameplay into one highly polished package," Daemon wrote. "You haven't played a game quite like this before and won't want to miss it."

Curry was perhaps best known for his role in the cult classic film The Rocky Horror Picture Show, but also appeared in many video games besides Brutal Legend, including Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 (back in the FMV cutscene days!), Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers, and Dragon Age: Origins.
Double Fine, meanwhile, has announced that it is using its newfound independence to bring back its Amnesia Fortnight game jam as it looks to create its next project(s).

highlights.title: Artist Yayoi Kusama Has Died at 97
highlights.summary: The renowned Japanese avant-gardist died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo from multiple organ failure, according to her US gallery, David Zwirner. She was 97.
body: Renowned Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo, according to her gallery, David Zwirner. She was 97. Kusama’s work, with its fizzy pop-culture style and preponderance of polka dots, spanned painting, drawing, sculpture, and performance, as well as literature, fashion, and product design. Her artworks regularly fetched record-breaking prices at auction.

Born in Matsumoto City, Japan, in 1929, Kusama studied Nihonga, a formal style of Japanese painting, in Kyoto. She began painting at the age of 10, with her early works reflecting hallucinogenic visions that often took the form of dots. The motif—which she later described as representing the cosmos—would become her signature. “After all, well, the moon is a polka dot, the sun is a polka dot, and then, the Earth where we live is also a polka dot,” she told a journalist.

Kusama moved to New York in 1957, attracted by the city’s experimental art scene. Over the next decade, she became part of the New York avant-garde, first attracting notice with her Infinity Nets, a series of artworks featuring undulating, apparently endless patterns.
points: The renowned Japanese avant-gardist died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tokyo from multiple organ failure, according to her US gallery, David Zwirner.
